html:
The Pech, once called Paya, are an Indigenous people of northeastern Honduras, in the river valleys and mountains of Olancho and Colón, inland from the Caribbean coast. Their language is Chibchan, related to languages of Costa Rica and Panama rather than to their Mesoamerican neighbours.

They grew manioc and maize and fished. On his fourth voyage in 1502, Columbus landed near Trujillo, on the coast they and their neighbours used. Spanish missions in the 1600s and 1700s, and raids by the Miskito, who sold captives to British traders, pushed them inland. Today a few thousand Pech live in small communities near the Tawahka and the Tolupan.
